independent/ASSESSMENT.md.text:
# Independent W015 assessment

The candidate passed both frozen independent cases.
The baseline passed neither gate criterion because it has no mechanical review gate.
This comparison supports the narrow command gate, not general workflow enforcement.
No blocking issue remains in the reviewed normal execution path.
Human adoption remains a separate decision.

## Frozen results

I01 changed the saved decision source after the first successful fake command.
The candidate stopped before a second command and created no run directory.
It preserved the first call and changed source bytes.
The baseline completed its synthetic run with 24 calls.

I02 changed the effective question after Pipeline construction.
The candidate stopped with zero calls and no run directory.
The baseline completed its synthetic run with 24 calls.
The source file and waiver remained unchanged in both versions.

The plan and fixture hashes were frozen before candidate inspection.
Those files still match their frozen hashes.
Both versions used the baseline's existing FakeTools.
No external tool process, network request, or account was used.

## Final code and retained runs

The first replay used candidate hash `c15349308a7cc74860ba126c60b5ed61d40c8141480b537051f8edbb36c02709`.
It passed both cases.
The worker then moved source symlink rejection before path resolution.
That order also handles symlink loops on Python 3.9.

The final replay used candidate hash `2e94c55101d855d7bf7219d7437821acd7e2221bc0e0c3c3ec263def1c54ba2c`.
Both versions repeated the same frozen cases with unchanged criteria.
The final candidate passed both cases again.
Keep `RESULTS.json` and `runs/` as the first replay evidence.
Use `RESULTS-final.json` and `runs-final/` for the final candidate.
The coordinator's saved suites also report 90 passing tests on Python 3.9.25 and 3.14.8.
The independent reviewer did not repeat those full suites.

## Covered execution path

`Pipeline.run()` checks the record before preflight or run-file changes.
Every command in the normal pipeline reaches the single runner invocation through `Pipeline.call()`.
That method checks the record immediately before invoking the runner.
The CLI execution path supplies the review log to the same Pipeline.
Plan mode has no new tool or file operation.

Validation binds the log to the effective configuration and run identity.
It rejects changed settings after construction.
It requires a strict event chain and valid source files for each event.
The latest event must be active, unexpired, and cover all required actions.
Denied calls preserve pending operation markers and query accounting.
The original export, response, and recovery protections remain in place.

## Exploratory boundary check

An additional probe called `Pipeline.call()` with a valid waiver and a different destination argument.
The FakeTools runner received that command.
This probe is separate from the frozen case counts.
Its evidence is in `COMMAND-SCOPE-PROBE.json`.

The gate checks record validity but does not authorize arbitrary command arguments.
The updated guide now states that normal `Pipeline.run()` generates commands from the bound configuration.
It also states that direct `Pipeline.call(args)` does not compare arbitrary arguments with that configuration.
This documentation matches the observed behavior.
No general command authorization mechanism is needed for this limited proposal.

## Remaining limits

Source files cannot prove the researcher's identity, consent, or intended meaning.
The gate cannot discover later decisions omitted from the supplied log.
An assistant can bypass it with direct tools, modified code, or changed permission files.
A concurrent change can occur after a check and before the checked command starts.
The gate cannot cancel an operation already in progress.

These checks used synthetic records and local fake commands.
They do not test real services, model compliance, or a full research project.
The supported interface now requires a waiver log for execution and recovery.
Planning remains available without one.

# Independent W015 checks

Freeze date: 2026-10-24.
Active review budget: 20 minutes.
The reviewer has read baseline code and the fixed evaluation cases.
The reviewer has not read candidate code.
Run only existing FakeTools in temporary local directories.
Do not use network access, accounts, or real external commands.

## I01: Source changes between commands

Create a valid full waiver for the exact effective configuration and run ID.
Call `Pipeline.run()` with an existing FakeTools wrapper.
After the first successful external command, append text to the waiver source file.
Leave the saved source hash and log unchanged.

The candidate must stop before a second external command starts.
The first command must remain in the recorded call list.
The source change must remain available for inspection.
The run directory must remain absent because the change occurs during preflight.
The baseline is expected to continue because it has no record gate.
Record the actual baseline behavior without changing the pass criteria.

## I02: Effective settings change after construction

Create a valid full waiver for the exact effective configuration and run ID.
Construct a Pipeline with those settings.
Change only `pipeline.settings["question"]` before calling `Pipeline.run()`.
Leave the waiver, saved source, and original configuration hash unchanged.

The candidate must stop before any external command starts.
It must not create the run directory.
This checks the direct Python API's binding to the settings it will use.
It does not claim resistance to deliberate code modification or direct tool use.
The baseline is expected to continue using the changed question.
Record the actual baseline behavior without changing the pass criteria.

## Shared evidence

Use fixtures in `fixtures/` for the configuration, source text, and case values.
Resolve the run directory under each fresh case directory.
Construct log bindings from that case's effective settings before each mutation.
Use an expiry in 2099 to avoid dependence on the current test date.
Record commands, exceptions, run files, effective settings, and source hashes.
Hash this plan and all frozen fixture files before candidate inspection.
Inspect the implementation after the coordinator sends its ready message.
Then report normal entry points and bypass limits separately.

These checks test cooperative mechanical behavior.
They do not authenticate researcher identity or consent.
They do not test real service behavior or model compliance.
